settings.bullet_1: Kneel on it, flip it, sit on it
settings.bullet_2: Handles help you stand back up
settings.set_blurb: A separate 10-piece set: folding stool, tool bag, six steel tools, claw gloves and a sprayer.

settings.heading: Kneel
settings.text: Set it pad-side up. Hold the handles as you go down.

settings.heading: Flip
settings.text: Turn it over. The snap-lock clicks and it is a stool.

settings.heading: Sit
settings.text: Rest on the seat for potting, weeding, or the mailbox.

settings.heading: The pad does the work your knees used to.
settings.text: Thick foam between you and the ground. Gravel, a wet lawn, a paved path, it makes no difference. You stay level and you stay dry.
settings.placeholder: Photo: hands on the handles, pushing up
settings.caption: Kneeling down in a bed. One take, no edit.
settings.points: Pad lifts off so you can hose it down | Wide flat feet, it does not sink into a lawn | Foam is [ PAD THICKNESS ] thick

settings.heading: Push up on the handles, then take it with you.
settings.text: Getting down is easy. Getting up is the part that hurts. The handles sit near hip height when you kneel, so your arms do the work instead of your knees. Then it comes with you to the next spot.
settings.placeholder: Photo: pad, close, coming off the frame
settings.caption: Standing up, then moving down the path.
settings.points: Carries in one hand, about [ WEIGHT ] | Folds flat and hangs in the shed | Steel frame, not plastic

settings.heading: Flip it and it is a stool.
settings.text: Same frame, upside down. The handles become the legs, the padded side becomes the seat. A snap-lock holds it closed so it will not fold while you are sitting on it.
settings.placeholder: Photo: folded flat, held by the handle
settings.caption: Working a raised bed, sitting on it.
settings.points: Snap-lock holds it shut | Holds up to [ WEIGHT CAPACITY ] | Nothing to swap or unscrew

settings.heading: Bad knees
settings.text: The pad keeps you off the ground. The handles take the strain when you get up.

settings.heading: Bad back
settings.text: Flip it and sit. Weeding and potting at bed height instead of bent double.

settings.heading: Anyone who hates getting up off the ground
settings.text: That is most of us past a certain age. Two handles and a frame fix it.

settings.question: How much weight does it hold?
settings.answer: The frame is rated to [ WEIGHT CAPACITY ].

settings.question: How heavy is it?
settings.answer: [ WEIGHT ]. Light enough to carry by the handle in one hand.

settings.question: Is there any assembly?
settings.answer: None. It arrives assembled. Take it out of the box and unfold it.

settings.question: Does it stay shut when I use it as a stool?
settings.answer: Yes. A snap-lock holds the frame shut when it is flipped. It clicks when it is locked.

settings.question: Will it sink into soft soil?
settings.answer: The feet are wide, so it sits well on lawn and on beds. On very soft ground, set it on the path or the grass edge.

settings.question: Can I leave it outside?
settings.answer: The frame is steel and handles weather. Bring the pad in when rain is coming so it does not soak through.

settings.question: How does shipping work?
settings.answer: Free shipping in the US. Most orders arrive in [ DELIVERY WINDOW ].

settings.question: The tool set has a stool too. Do I need both?
settings.answer: They do different jobs. The kneeler is padded, has handles to push up on, and flips between kneeling and sitting. The stool in the tool set is a light canvas seat that carries the tool bag out to the bed. Plenty of people run both, which is what the bundles are for.

settings.question: What if it is not for me?
settings.answer: Send it back within 30 days for a refund.
